savings.reason: Read the complete original EO:13028, both held actor contexts, and the full EO:13345 sections 1-7. Section 6 unconditionally revokes the parent EO:12757 and EO:13028; no savings, accrued-rights preservation or exception continues this order's operative force. Successor foreign-affairs delegations and Board rules in EO:13345 sections 1-5 rest on that new order and do not save the former order. The judicial-review limitation concerns rights under this order and does not independently continue the revoked delegations or amendment commands. The bounded OFR later-instrument and eCFR searches are adequate for this no-order claim; no affirmative revival or residual lead is present.

research_rationale: Read the complete official original EO:13028 and full EO:13131 and EO:13345 actor texts. The corrected inventory retains each operative section 1 amendment (two preamble changes, three section 1 changes, redesignation, and the new prospective section-571 reference rule) and the independent section 2 judicial-review limitation, without duplicating introductory scaffolding or including page furniture. EO:13131 adds Tropical Forest authority, changes punctuation at other preamble/section-1 locations, and alters parent sections 3-4; it does not repeal the inserted section-571 delegations, their consultation requirements, the redesignation or the prospective-reference rule. Its inserted words after Public Law 102-549 coexist with EO:13028's different insertion; neither order replaces that whole preamble. These are partial amendments, not an earlier termination of the retained original clauses. The dossier missing-list entries are assessed individually: EO:12823 predates EO:13028 and is acknowledged as the parent's existing amendment history, so it cannot be a later end of EO:13028's independent commands; the supposed missing EO:13131 provision is cured substantively by the full held actor context. No own-term sunset or report deadline is present. A condition on later matching statutes in inserted section 6 changes reference scope; it does not end the order upon a particular event. EO:13345 section 6(c), in a full actor dated July 8, 2004, immediately says the order is hereby revoked; no postponed effective clause is present. The July 13 Federal Register publication and July 12 filing dates do not control this unconditional internal-government revocation. The full original and actor contain no savings continuing this order. OFR catalog/held-order search covers named later dispositions and operative sentences, supplemented by the cutoff eCFR search. The U.S. Code search through October 9 is not used to assert a current predicate. No conflicts or affirmative revival leads remain.
